{{NSE|TNPL}} | founded = 1979 | hq_location = [[Chennai]], [[Karur]], [[Manapparai]], [[Tiruchirappalli]] | owner = [[Government of Tamil Nadu]] | parent = [[Department of Industries (Tamil Nadu)]] | key_people = Dr. M. Sai Kumar, I.A.S.
(Chairman & Managing Director){{cite web|url=https://www.tnpl.com/leadership |title=Leadership |website=tnpl.com |access-date=2024-05-18}} | industry = Bagasse-based [[paper mill]] | revenue = {{decrease}} {{INRConvert|39.58|b}} (2020){{cite web|url=https://tnpl.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/Investor/Financial_Reporting/Annual_Reports/Download-Annual-Reports-2019-20.pdf| title=Annual Report 2019-20 | publisher= TNPL. | date=6 November 2020 | accessdate= 6 November 2020}} | net_income = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|1.30|b}} (2020) | assets = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|40.39|b}} (2020) | equity = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|17.13|b}} (2020) | num_employees = 2567 (2020) | website = {{URL|http://www.tnpl.com/}} }} [[File:Mill view 2 large.jpg|thumb|right|Mill view of TNPL, [[Karur]]]] The '''Tamil Nadu Newsprint and Papers Limited''' ('''TNPL'''){{cite web |author= |title=TNPL's Official Website |url=http://www.tnpl.com/Index.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090410075347/http://www.tnpl.com/Index.aspx |archive-date=10 April 2009 |accessdate=29 June 2010 |website=Tamil Nadu Newsprint and Papers Limited}} is a company that was established by the [[Government of Tamil Nadu]]{{cite web |author= |date=6 June 2005 |title=Tamil Nadu Newsprint And Papers Limited Citizen's Charter |url=http://www.tn.gov.in/citizen/tnpl.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100125163240/http://www.tn.gov.in/citizen/tnpl.html |archive-date=25 January 2010 |accessdate=29 June 2010 |website=Government of Tamil Nadu}} to produce newsprint and writing paper using [[bagasse]], a [[sugarcane]] residue. The Government of Tamil Nadu listed the paper mill in April 1979 under the provisions of the Companies Act of 1956. The factory is situated at [[TNPL Pugalur|Kagithapuram]] in the [[Karur District]] of [[Tamil Nadu]] and Manapparai, Trichy district of Tamil Nadu. The registered office of the company is located in [[Guindy]], [[Chennai]]. ==History== The company commenced production in 1984 with an initial capacity of 90,000 tonnes per annum. TNPL started the commercial production of newsprint on its new Paper Machine No. 2 in January 1996. The machine was supplied by Voith Sulzer Paper Technology{{cite web | url=http://www.voithpaper.com/media/vp_en_twogether_7.pdf | author =Voith Sulzer Paper Technology |title=Voith Paper Media Release (Refer Page.No14) | accessdate=29 June 2010}} and its licensee in India, [[Larsen & Toubro|Larsen and Toubro Limited]], and has opened up vistas for newsprint making. ==Technology and process== TNPL has ventured with nearby sugar mills such as Sakthi Sugar Mills for continued supply of Bagasse for the Paper mill where steam will be provided to the sugar mill in exchange of bagasse.{{cite web |author= |date=8 June 2002 |title=TNPL: Turning Over A New Leaf |url=http://www.financialexpress.com/news/tnpl-turning-over-a-new-leaf/48659/0 |accessdate=29 June 2010}} ==Quality standards== TNPL has obtained the ISO 9001:2000 certification from RWTÜV{{cite web | url=http://www.rwtuev.de/e/1754|title=RWTÜV, "TÜV" technical inspection organization | author= RWTÜV Official Site | accessdate=29 June 2010}} of Germany for the development and supply of newsprint and papers. TNPL is accredited with ISO 14001:2004 certification. ===TNPL Effluent Water Lift Irrigation Society (TEWLIS)=== Under the TNPL Effluent Water Lift Irrigation Scheme is intended to provide farmers effluent water for irrigation purpose. The treated effluent water is used to irrigate about {{convert|1250|acre|km2|adj=on}} of dry land with about 250 farmers of the TNPL Effluent Water Lift Irrigation Society. The effluents have to comply with the norms set by the [[Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board]]. ===TNPL Plantation Programme=== TNPL has developed plantations in 2004–2005 and launched two plantation schemes, namely Farm Forestry and Captive Plantation.{{cite web |author=Balaji |first=R. |date=5 June 2010 |title=TNPL sees two key efforts cutting costs this year |url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/2010/06/06/stories/2010060650250200.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100611103028/http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/2010/06/06/stories/2010060650250200.htm |archive-date=11 June 2010 |accessdate=29 June 2010 |website=The Hindu Business Line}} Captive plantations are raised on lands owned by companies, government departments, and educational institutions on a revenue-sharing basis or on a lease-rent basis. The minimum criteria for captive plantations is that the land should be a block of {{convert|25|acre|m2}} and above in a single location. In the last five years of operation (2004–05 to 2008–09), TNPL has raised plantations in {{convert|37556|acre|km2}} involving 8235 farmers in twenty-eight districts in Tamil Nadu under the Farm Forestry scheme and {{convert|2735|acre|km2}} under the Captive Plantation Scheme. TNPL has planted pulpwood on about 40,291 acres of land (as of 31 March 2009).{{cite news |author=Renganathan |first=L. |date=5 February 2010 |title=TNPL harvests benefits |url=http://www.hindu.com/2010/02/05/stories/2010020556690100.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100209194227/http://www.hindu.com/2010/02/05/stories/2010020556690100.htm |archive-date=9 February 2010 |accessdate=29 June 2010 |work=[[The Hindu]] |location=Chennai, India}} === Clonal propagation and research center === TNPL established a clonal propagation and research center.{{cite news |author=Renganathan |first=L. |date=28 January 2008 |title=New clonal research centre inaugurated |url=http://www.hindu.com/2008/01/28/stories/2008012856300100.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080128171803/http://www.hindu.com/2008/01/28/stories/2008012856300100.htm |archive-date=28 January 2008 |accessdate=29 June 2010 |work=[[The Hindu]] |location=Chennai, India}} The clonal production centre was started with a mini clonal hedge garden of {{Convert|4000|m2|abbr=on}}, a mist chamber of {{Convert|8000|m2|abbr=on}}, and {{Convert|20000|m2|abbr=on}} of open nursery. The production center was established at an outlay of about 50 million. The plantation schemes are being implemented throughout Tamil Nadu through 10 regional offices in Karur, Manaparai, Tirunelveli, Karaikudi, Pudukottai, Namakkal, Trichy, Tanjore, Jayangondam, and Panruti. === Forestry research and development === TNPL has partnered with the [[Indian Council of Agricultural Research#Organization|NAIP-ICAR]]-sponsored project titled "A value chain on industrial Agro-forestry in Tamil Nadu" for the promotion of tree husbandry with improved short-rotation clones and [[genotype]]s through [[contract farming]]. {{cite web |author=National Agricultural Innovation Project, ICAR |date=2 September 2008 |title=Value Chain on Industrial Agroforestry in Tamil Nadu |url=http://www.naip.icar.org.in/ES/ESC2TNAUAgroforestry.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721180831/http://www.naip.icar.org.in/ES/ESC2TNAUAgroforestry.pdf |archive-date=21 July 2011 |accessdate=29 June 2010 |df=dmy-all}} Forest College & Research Institute (FC & RI), Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Mettupalayam is the Consortium Leader of this project. This project is being implemented to raise {{convert|500|acre|km2}} of cluster plantation in 10 [[Tehsil|taluks]] covering 5 districts in Tamil Nadu. TNPL has obtained the [[ISO 14000#ISO 14001 standard|ISO 14001]] certification from RMTUV, Germany. TNPL has commissioned the [[Biomethanation|bio-methanation]] plant, which generates around 23,000 m3 of [[biogas]] (methane) per day, to be used as fuel in the lime-kiln in place of [[furnace oil]]. The biogas replaces around 10–12 kiloliters of furnace oil per day in the lime-kiln. In 2003–2004, the bio-methanation plant generated 4,145,000 m3 of [[methane]] gas. TNPL also obtained the ''3 Leaves Award''{{cite web |author=TNPL awarded Three Green Leaves by Centre for Science and Environment (1 January 2009) |title=Pulp and Paper Sector: Rating Scorecard 1 |url=https://www.cseindia.org/node/285 |accessdate=6 July 2010}} under the Green Rating project of the [[Centre for Science and Environment]], New Delhi, in October 2004. ==Energy management policy== TNPL has installed its own power generating facility through the installation of 61.18 MW power generating equipment (TG Sets) installed at the paper mill site and the 18 MW [[wind farm]] installed at [[Devarkulam (Tirunelveli)|Devarkulam]] and Perungudi of [[Tirunelveli district]]. The surplus power generated is being exported to the State Grid. The wind farm capacity was changed to 21.75 MW in March 2004 by installing 3 wind turbine generators of 1250 kW capacity each. It has installed a bio-methanation plant to generate methane gas from the effluent water (bagasse wash water) and use it as fuel as a substitute for furnace oil in the lime kiln. In 2004–2005, TNPL generated 3,412,000 m3 methane gas. The Indian Industry has recognised the project as an ''Innovative Project''. == Registered projects == ===Methane extraction project=== TNPL commissioned a special kind of reactor concept for the "high rate" anaerobic treatment of an [[Upflow anaerobic sludge blanket digestion|upflow anaerobic sludge blanket]] (UASB) reactor, which uses anaerobic granular sludge bed technology. The project also involves a system for extracting biogas from the closed reactor as fuel in a [[lime kiln]], which had been using furnace oil.{{cite web | url=http://cdm.unfccc.int/Projects/DB/DNV-CUK1131389672.69| title= CDM Benefits for Methane Extraction and Fuel Conservation | author= United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) | accessdate=29 June 2010}}{{cite news | url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/news-by-industry/indl-goods-/-svs/paper-/-wood-/-glass/-plastic/-marbles/TNPL-into-carbon-trading/articleshow/1905930.cms|title= TNPL into carbon trading | author= Economic Times (18 August 2006) | accessdate=29 June 2010 | work=The Times of India | date=18 August 2006}} ===6.75 MW Small Scale Grid Connected Wind Electricity Generation Project=== [[File:TNPL windmill1.jpg|thumb|right|Wind generators of TNPL (extreme right) at Devarkulam, [[Tirunelveli]], [[Tamil Nadu]], India.]] TNPL has generated energy. The project activity involves the installation, operation and maintenance of seven grid connected wind electricity generators (WEG) owned by the project proponent, TNPL. The electricity generated from the seven WEGs will be exported to the [[TNEB|Tamil Nadu Electricity Board]] (TNEB) grid. The seven WEGs have been installed in two phases.{{cite web |author= |date=1 April 2004 |title=Project 1053 : 6.75 MW Small Scale Grid Connected "Wind Electricity Generation Project" by Tamil Nadu Newsprint and Papers Limited |url=http://cdm.unfccc.int/Projects/DB/DNV-CUK1175246467.05/iProcess |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150407033708/https://cdm.unfccc.int/Projects/DB/DNV-CUK1175246467.05/iProcess |archive-date=7 April 2015 |accessdate=29 June 2010 |website=United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change}} The first phase involved installation of four [[NEG Micon]] 750 kW WEGs and the second phase involved the erection of three [[Suzlon Energy]] WEGs of 1.25 MW. On 30 March 2001, TNPL commenced operations for the first phase of the project with the installation of the four 750 kW WEGs. The second phase of the project commenced operations in March 2004.{{cite web |author=Vazquez |first=Tatiana |date=14 May 2020 |title=TNPL to expand wind farm capacity |url=http://www.blonnet.com/2005/08/24/stories/2005082402740200.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200927132406/https://hypernoir.com/francia-aprueba-ley-que-obliga-a-las-plataformas-en-linea-a-eliminarcontenido-de-discurso-de-odio-dentro-de-las-24-horas/ |archive-date=27 September 2020 |accessdate=29 June 2010 |website=Hypernoir |language=es}} All seven WEGs have been installed in the [[Tirunelveli|Thirunelveli]] district, in the state of Tamil Nadu, India. ===Savings=== {| class="wikitable" ! |} ==Products== The paper produced by TNPL is subjected to [[Elemental Chlorine Free|elemental chlorine-free]] (ECF) bleaching. The paper is acid-free. TNPL manufactures papers in substances ranging from 50 [[Grams per square metre|GSM]] to 90 GSM. Newsprint is normally manufactured in 49 Gsm ([[Grammage|grams per square meter]]) reels and directly sold by the company to various newspaper establishments such as ''[[The Hindu]]'', ''[[Malayala Manorama]]'', ''Ananda Bazaar Patrika'', and others. The printing and writing paper is manufactured in reel and sheet forms, with the Gsm varying from 50 to 80. === Export network === TNPL is also exporting about 18% of the PWP production to 20 countries. {{div col|colwidth=15em}} * Australia * Egypt * Greece * Indonesia * Jordan * Kenya * Malaysia * Myanmar * Nepal * Nigeria * Philippines * Singapore * Sri Lanka * Sudan * South Africa * Taiwan * Turkey * U.A.E * UK * United States * Yemen {{div col end}} The "[[World Wide Fund]]" has entered into a pact with TNPL to use the "Panda" logo in its branded products. ==Controversy== On 14 September 2009, the General Farmers' Association of Pugalur, the Pugalur Consumer Protection Council, and the Pugalur Channel Aycutdars' Association alleged that the TNPL's release of effluents into the channel has caused the public in the area to be "afraid of the ill effects of the effluents".{{cite news |title=Farmers allege pollution of Pugalur channel |url=http://www.hindu.com/2009/09/18/stories/2009091856540300.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130125085552/http://www.hindu.com/2009/09/18/stories/2009091856540300.htm |archive-date=25 January 2013 |accessdate=5 July 2010 |work=[[The Hindu]] |location=Chennai, India}} === Response === The TNPL has claimed that no effluent was being let into the Pugalur Channel, as alleged. TNPL Managing Director Mohammed Nasimuddin stated that "The TNPL has implemented a Mill Development Plan at a capital outlay of {{INR}}6 billion mainly for incorporating various environmental improvement measures such as switching over to Elemental Chlorine Free Bleaching and reduction in water consumption. In this system the use of chlorine is totally eliminated and the bleaching is carried out only by [[chlorine dioxide]]".{{Citation needed|date=May 2024}} == Shareholding == The [[government of Tamil Nadu]] listed TNPL shares in the following organizations: :* [[Bombay Stock Exchange]] :* [[National Stock Exchange of India]] :* [[National Securities Depository Limited]] :* [[Central Depository Services Limited]] :* [[Debenture Trustees – Vijaya Bank]] TNPL became a share market listed company from the year 1997. The government of Tamil Nadu declared TNPL as "Other Companies" list from the previous "Government of Tamil Nadu's Public Sector Undertakings" list after 1997. The government holds 35.32% of equity shares in TNPL as of 31 March 2012.{{Cite web |title=Share Holding Pattern |url=http://www.tnpl.com/DisplayPage.aspx?file=share_holding.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160308113048/http://www.tnpl.com/DisplayPage.aspx?file=share_holding.htm |archive-date=8 March 2016 |access-date=15 May 2024 |website=Tamil Nadu Newsprint and Papers Limited}} == Management == *Thiru. extract: The Tamil Nadu Newsprint and Papers Limited (TNPL) is a company that was established by the Government of Tamil Nadu to produce newsprint and writing paper using bagasse, a sugarcane residue. The Government of Tamil Nadu listed the paper mill in April 1979 under the provisions of the Companies Act of 1956. The factory is situated at Kagithapuram  in the Karur District of Tamil Nadu and Manapparai, Trichy district of Tamil Nadu. The registered office of the company is located in Guindy, Chennai.
